title: Resolve answer
description: The body of the adapter's signed 200 answer to the call with the path resolve (resolve.schema.json), application/json: one result for each address of the call, in the call's order. The control plane refuses an answer whose results do not list the call's addresses one for one, in that order, a rule the schema cannot express. The answer is signed with the adapter's access key, bound to the call's signature, as definitions.schema.json describes an answer to a call, and contains the revision it was built for in revision. The adapter has one access key for every organisation, and no call but a call with the path run-credential whose purpose is work contains a connection_id, so a resolve result can contain a grant_ref of a connection of another organisation. The control plane uses a resolve result only under a grant that the run may use: a grant of a live connection of the run's organisation; or, only to read a harness source and only with access read, a grant whose organisation assigned that source to the run's organisation, at that version and at that path or export. The control plane also uses a result with public: true without a grant, and then only to read the resource with the call with the path read-public, with the result's public_ref as resource_ref (read-public.schema.json). Under an assignment, the control plane sends a call with the path run-credential only when the credential_scope of the adapter's description is resource, which it also is when absent (description.schema.json), and with resources set to the resource_ref of the assigned source alone; when credential_scope is grant, the control plane sends no call with the path run-credential under an assignment, and reads the assigned source only with the call with the path read. A harness source is a remote source that the run's harness extends or takes a module from, whether that harness is the harness file of the target or the harness member of the run documents (run/v1 documents.schema.json). An assignment never covers a call with the path run-credential whose purpose is work or whose access is write: work access comes only from a grant of a live connection of the run's organisation. The control plane treats every other resolve result as covered: false, or, when the result has public: true, as a result with public: true and no grant_ref, so nothing that a run of one organisation receives shows that another organisation holds a grant for that address. The control plane sends a call with the path read, and a call with the path run-credential whose purpose is harness, only under a grant that the run may use, and sends a call with the path run-credential whose purpose is work only with the connection_id of the collections of the call's resources, which is a live connection of the run's organisation when the call is sent. The control plane sends a call with the path read-public only with resource_ref set to the public_ref of a resolve result with public: true, never with the resource_ref of a covered result, and never sends a call with the path run-credential for a resource that it reads with the call with the path read-public: reading a public resource gives the run no credential. The control plane ignores a member that this schema does not define, unless the must_understand of the answer lists it. It refuses an answer whose must_understand lists a pointer that it does not define.

version.description: The document format. The control plane refuses a version it does not read.

revision.description: The contract revision the adapter built the answer for, the one in the call's X-Qory-Contract-Version. The control plane refuses an answer whose revision is not the call's.

results.description: One result for each address of the call, in the call's order.

must_understand.description: The members of the document that the reader must understand, each as a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) counted from the document, such as /results. List each once, at most 32. A pointer has no line feed, and writes ~ only as ~0 or ~1. Each pointer is to a member that this schema defines. The control plane ignores a member that this schema does not define, unless the must_understand of the answer lists it. It refuses an answer whose must_understand lists a pointer that it does not define.

result.description: The result for one address, in one of three forms: grant_ref and resource_ref, the grant and the resource at the source that cover it, which may also contain public: true and public_ref when the source shows that resource without a credential; public: true, resource_ref and public_ref, with no grant_ref, which the adapter may answer when no grant it holds covers the address and the source shows the resource without a credential; or covered: false, when the adapter cannot read the address, or no grant it holds covers it and the adapter does not answer public: true for it, and then no grant_ref, resource_ref, public or public_ref. The control plane sends the call with the path read-public with the result's public_ref, never with the resource_ref of a covered result.

address.description: The address, exactly as the call wrote it.

grant_ref.description: The grant that covers the address, as the adapter reported it (grant.schema.json). Absent from a result with public: true when no grant the adapter holds covers the address.

resource_ref.description: The adapter's ref to the resource at the address, stable for that resource. The control plane compares it and stores it, and never reads meaning into it.

covered.description: false: no grant the adapter holds covers the address, and the adapter does not answer public: true for it.

public_ref.description: The ref of the resource at the address that a request without a credential, under no grant, can use, such as a host followed by a path: the ref that the control plane sends as resource_ref in the call with the path read-public (read-public.schema.json). Present exactly when public is true. In a result with no grant_ref, it may be equal to resource_ref. The control plane compares it and stores it, and never reads meaning into it.

public.description: true: the source shows the resource at the address to anyone without a credential. A result may contain it, and an adapter answers public: true only if it serves the call with the path read-public (read-public.schema.json). The adapter decides it from the visibility of the resource as a request without a credential sees it at the moment of the call, never from a grant it holds. A resource that the source shows only to signed-in users is not public. Absent, the control plane treats the resource as not public.
